idiom_name: MikroORM EntityManager identity map with per-request fork (AsyncLocalStorage)
implementation_notes: In the Node ecosystem the identity map arrives with the ORM: MikroORM's EntityManager keeps one instance per entity, so a row fetched twice yields the same object (jon === all[0] holds), and it refuses a global context - you fork an EntityManager per request (orm.em.fork()) or open a RequestContext built on node:async_hooks AsyncLocalStorage so every lookup resolves to the request-scoped map. The classic structure is therefore replaced by the forked EntityManager plus em.clear() when the request ends; without an identity-map ORM (Prisma, Sequelize), hand-write a Map keyed by id in the repository and accept that identity only holds along the paths you route through it.
pitfalls: Using the global EntityManager is a global identity map: stale entities across requests plus unbounded memory - fork per request (allowGlobalContext only for tests).
The AsyncLocalStorage context must exist before the ORM is used in the request pipeline (register the middleware late, after body parsing) or lookups escape to the global context.
The identity map is not a result cache: it lives within one request and must not be reused across requests.
